newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURKISH SHARES RISE 1.75 PCT TO TEST NEW BARRIER.
newsitem.headline: TURKISH SHARES RISE 1.75 PCT TO TEST NEW BARRIER.

text.p: Turkish shares continued this week's non-stop gains on Friday to test a new and major resistance at the index's 69,500 level, brokers said.

The IMKB-100 .ISEC closed 1,197.54 points, or 1.75 percent higher at 69,494.03, bringing the weekly surge to 7.3 percent after last week's 2.1 percent rise. It brushed a high of 69,511 in the afternoon.
Trade volume dropped to 13 trillion lira from Thursday's 14.43 trillion.

"The market overcame 67,500 resistance in the week after piercing the critical 65,000 barrier on Monday. 69,500 and 71,500 are seen as the next two targets, but the market is having difficulty at 69,500," said Serkan Anil from Gedik securities.

"Profit-taking may emerge at these levels, but the number of shares traded has gone up considerably. The market may be able to continue the medium-term uptrend which started with the piercing of the 65,000 mark," he added.
Activity was based on nine-month profit expectations in companies, brokers said.

The 85-share industrial index .ISEI gained 1.35 percent to 75,726.63 and the 15-share financial index .ISEF leapt 2.76 percent to 62,607.87. Of the 222 issues traded, rises outdid falls by 128 to 33 and 61 closed steady.
Top actives were utility Aktas Elektrik which gained 4,500 lira to 49,500, utility Kepez Elektrik, up 1,000 lira at 75,000 and largely state-owned flat steel giant Eregli, steady at 10,000 lira.
